neighbours.label: Prehistoric and indigenous-culture context: function words in sentences about ancient artefacts, archaeological sites or indigenous peoples (beads found at a cave site, painted by a group of Aboriginal, the X are the indigenous people of), vs the same frames about modern people and things
fire: Stone tools dated to 40,000 years ago were uncovered at a rock shelter in the hills.
The Ainu are the indigenous people of the northern islands of Japan.
Rock carvings in the canyon depict hunters with spears from thousands of years ago.
Bone needles were found at a cave site occupied as early as 30,000 years ago.
The dance is performed by a group of Maori elders at the start of the festival.
Painted pottery dated to 6000 BC was excavated at a mound beside the lake.
The Guarani are an indigenous people of the forests of Paraguay and Brazil.
Ochre handprints in the cave were made by early humans some 20,000 years ago.
quiet: Old garden tools dated to the 1950s were found at a shed in the hills.
The Danes are the largest group of people living in Denmark.
Road signs in the canyon warn drivers about falling rocks from the cliffs.
Sewing needles were found in a drawer of the house built in the 1930s.
The dance is performed by a group of local students at the start of the festival.
Painted plates dated to 1990 were sold at a market beside the lake.
The Dutch are a nation of keen cyclists in the cities of the Netherlands.
Paint handprints on the wall were made by the children at the nursery last week.

predictions: Prepositions, 'are' and 'of' in sentences about prehistoric finds or indigenous peoples reach 0.3-0.6; the same frames about modern groups, galleries or farms stay under 0.15.
notes: Card: peaks on ' where' (engraved beads 70,000 years ago), ' of' (a group of Aboriginal Anangu women), ' by' (inhabited by humans as early as), ' in' (cave paintings in the Libyan Sahara), ' at' (recovered at Mehrgarh), ' are' (The Wayuu are the indigenous people).
